summary: Langlade County tower listed as gone. 1931 newspaper items report a fatal collapse, placed at Lake Ada in one and at Eader Lake in another. Matching the regional Lake Ada page to the list entry is an assumption.

facts.status_note: Listed as Gone on the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Wisconsin list.

events.note: Collapse of the Lake Ada fire tower, reported as killing one man (May 8, 1931 item); cause not stated. A separate April 29, 1931 item reports a fatal tower collapse at Eader Lake; the page does not say whether it is the same event.

evidence.quote: George Coplan, 45, fire ranger, is dead today, crushed and killed instantly when a sudden wind collapsed a 100-foot observation tower at the Eader Lake lookout station in Forest county.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no build date, staffing, owner or removal date found. The Central US 'Lake Ada' page is assumed to be the same tower as firelookout 'Ada Lake' (same county and name); that page gives no coordinates. The two 1931 items name different sites: the April 29 item places a fatal collapse at Eader Lake (Forest County, cited to the Capital Times on the page), the May 8 item reports a fatal collapse at the Lake Ada tower (cited to the Oshkosh Daily Northwestern on the page). Nothing on the page says whether they describe one collapse or two, so the story reports both and does not link them. Both are secondhand transcriptions on the regional site; the original newspapers were not checked. Suggested next steps: 1931 newspaper archives for both items, and Chequamegon-Nicolet or Langlade County historical records for construction and removal. A search snippet mentioned a Lakewood/Laona Ranger District volunteer listing for a campground; not verified, not used.
